page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical AMD EPYC 9T34 cores running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. This single-threaded strength is reflected in high-tier performance for image and text processing, as well as Passmark CPU encryption tests. In contrast, multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with database operations and Redis SET throughput, also demonstrate average tier performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g8ae.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads that require strong single-thread execution alongside moderate multi-threaded capacity. The absence of local storage reduces base hardware costs but necessitates external storage planning. This profile is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, web serving, application servers, and moderate database operations that do not require local NVMe drives or GPU acceleration.

It features a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. However, multi-core metrics and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. This resource profile makes the ecs.g8ae.8xlarge highly suitable for general-purpose enterprise applications, web serving, and software compilation workloads that benefit from high single-thread efficiency without requiring local SSD storage or GPU acceleration.
